A draft; change it by consensus.

<span id="voice"></span>
== Voice ==

* Plain and direct. The movement voice belongs in [[About]] and [[Communications]]; reference and how-to pages stay neutral.
* Address the reader as “you” and the collective as “we”.

<span id="claims"></span>
== Claims ==

* Say what is '''shipped''' and what is '''planned'''. Never describe planned work as working.
* Date anything that changes (“as of 23 November 2026”), and link to the source of truth, usually a project README.
* Do not call a project production-ready, certified or 1:1 compatible unless its own README says so.
* Use vendor names only to describe compatibility. Do not imply affiliation.

<span id="formatting"></span>
== Formatting ==

* Sentence-case headings and page titles.
* Start each page with a sentence saying what it is. Put the most useful content first.
* Use tables for comparisons and short lists for steps.
* Link the first mention of a concept on a page.
* Link to the landing page of the section the page belongs to.
* Mark a gap with <code>TODO: needs input from &lt;who&gt;</code>, and keep the list of open items at the bottom of the page.

<span id="sources-and-provenance"></span>
== Sources and provenance ==

* Cite where a fact came from (README, website page, standards document).
* For anything about a vendor’s product, only use public sources. See [[Rules of the road]].
